text: {"question":"How does the empirical determination of helium abundance from the LBT project influence the comparison between cosmological constraints derived from the CMB and those that rely on theoretical BBN predictions, and what role does this play when considering the impact of deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio measurements on models that aim to resolve the Hubble tension?","reference_answer":"The LBT project’s empirical helium measurement allows CMB‑derived cosmological parameters to be calibrated directly from observation rather than from theoretical BBN, yielding constraints comparable to those obtained with standard BBN assumptions. This empirical approach becomes crucial when deuterium‑to‑hydrogen ratio data—used to tighten Ω_b h^2 bounds—are incorporated, as it helps assess whether models that relax the Hubble tension remain consistent with both observed helium and deuterium abundances."}
